title: Motion Verbs 9: Mixed Review
description: Synthesis of the motion-verb track. The pair-choice (one-way vs round-trip), the destination preposition (в / на + acc), and all five prefixes (по-, при-, у-, вы-, в-) come together. The student names the framework operating in each sentence and builds full motion sentences.
descriptionRussian: Итоговое повторение трека «Глаголы движения». В одном уроке встречаются выбор пары (одно- или разнонаправленные глаголы), предлоги направления (в / на + винительный) и все пять приставок (по-, при-, у-, вы-, в-). Ученик определяет, какая система действует в каждом предложении, и сам строит предложения о движении.
intro: Five questions in order and any motion sentence resolves. On foot or by vehicle. One way or round trip. Which moment of the journey. Then the destination preposition, then the source. Nothing here is new; what is new is running all five without stopping, which is what speaking actually requires.
rules: Step 1: foot or transport. Идти / ходить on foot; ехать / ездить by transport. The diagnostic is the manner of travel, not the destination.
Step 2: one-way or round-trip. Идти / ехать = single one-way trip in progress (сейчас); ходить / ездить = round-trip, habit, or general claim (часто, вчера-and-back).

Step 3: which moment of the trip. In-progress (шёл, ехал), round-trip (ходил, ездил), onset (пошёл, поехал), arrival (пришёл, приехал), gone-away (ушёл, уехал), exit (вышел, выехал), entry (вошёл, въехал).
Step 4: destination preposition. В + acc for enclosed spaces (buildings, cities, parks); на + acc for events and idiomatic places (работа, почта, стадион).
Step 5: source phrase. Из + gen for buildings and cities; с + gen for surfaces and daily-life activities. Source phrases pair with при-, у-, and вы-.
examples: Маша часто ходит в музей по выходным. (Masha often goes to the museum on weekends.) Round-trip / habit, foot, в + acc.
Антон уже ушёл с работы. (Anton has already left work.) Gone-away, foot, с + gen source.
Дети вошли в класс и сели на места. (The kids walked into the classroom and took their seats.) Entry, foot, в + acc, sequence inside.
Иван приехал из Москвы вчера. (Ivan arrived from Moscow yesterday.) Arrival, transport, из + gen source.
Лена пошла домой сразу после работы. (Lena left for home right after work.) Onset, foot, домой destination.
Машина выехала из города рано утром. (The car drove out of the city early in the morning.) Exit, transport, из + gen source.

rows.label: One-way or round-trip
cells: cue family (сейчас, часто, в этот момент)

rows.label: Gone away
cells: subject no longer at speaker's location

rows.label: Exit (specific space)
cells: moment of crossing out of a bounded space

rows.label: Entry (specific space)
cells: moment of crossing into a bounded space

items.prompt: Иван _____ в офис в девять часов и сразу поздоровался.
items.promptEnglish: Ivan walked into the office at nine and immediately greeted everyone.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 8: 'и сразу поздоровался' is a sequence inside the office. Which prefix matches the threshold reading?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 8: 'и сразу поздоровался' is the threshold + immediate-action pattern that pulls в-. Masc past of войти → вошёл. Шёл would describe motion in progress, not the threshold; пошёл would mark only setting off; пришёл would report arrival without the into-the-space focus. Recognising the cue family is the meta-skill this synthesis lesson targets.

items.prompt: Когда Маша _____ домой, она встретила старого друга.
items.promptEnglish: When Masha was walking home, she met an old friend.
items.hint: 'Когда X шла, Y' frames a moment within a single in-progress trip. Which form?
items.explanation: 'Когда X шла, Y' is the canonical in-progress past frame: a moment is captured inside a single one-way trip. Bare past of идти, fem → шла. The meeting interrupts the walk; it does not require a completed trip. Ходила would mean a round-trip; пошла would mark setting off; пришла would put her at home, missing the mid-trip moment.

items.prompt: Вчера Антон _____ в кино с друзьями.
items.promptEnglish: Yesterday Anton went to the cinema with friends (and came back).
items.hint: 'Вчера X в кино' frames a completed round-trip: he went and is back. Which form?
items.explanation: 'Вчера X в кино' is the canonical past round-trip frame: the speaker reports a completed there-and-back. Bare past of ходить, masc → ходил. Шёл would describe motion in progress at some past moment; пошёл would mark only the moment of setting off; пришёл would put him at the cinema as endpoint. Only the round-trip reading covers both legs.

items.prompt: Лена _____ из Москвы вчера вечером и привезла подарки.
items.promptEnglish: Lena arrived from Moscow yesterday evening and brought gifts.
items.hint: 'Из + gen' source plus 'привезла подарки': she is back here. Which transport prefix?
items.explanation: The 'из Москвы' source phrase + 'привезла подарки' (she brought gifts here) confirm Lena is back at the speaker's location: arrival reading. Fem past of приехать → приехала. Уехала would mean she left for somewhere else; поехала the moment of setting off; ехала her in transit. Only приехала hosts the gift-bringing-back framing.

items.prompt: Дети уже _____ в школу час назад.
items.promptEnglish: The kids already left for school an hour ago.
items.hint: 'Уже... час назад' + the implicit 'they are not here.' Plural absence-focus on foot?
items.explanation: 'Уже' + 'час назад' anchors the absence: the kids left and have not come back to the speaker's location. Plural past of уйти → ушли. Пошли would mark only the moment of setting off, but the 'уже ... час назад' framing pulls the gone-away reading. Пришли would put them at school; ходили would describe a completed round-trip with no clear absence focus.

items.prompt: Машина _____ из города рано утром на трассу.
items.promptEnglish: The car drove out of the city early in the morning onto the highway.
items.hint: 'Из города... на трассу' names a threshold-crossing on transport. Which prefix?
items.explanation: 'Из города' (bounded source) + 'на трассу' (onto an open transit destination) names the threshold of city limits. Threshold reading on transport → выехала (fem past of выехать). Уехала would frame a long absence with no threshold focus; поехала would mark setting off; ехала would describe motion in progress.

items.hint: She is HERE now, and Moscow is the source.
items.explanation: Arrival takes при-: приехала из Москвы. Уехала would mean she left and is gone; поехала marks departure; ездила a completed round trip.

items.promptEnglish: Anton has already left for work.
items.hint: He is gone from here; work is where he headed.
items.explanation: The away-from-here reading takes у-: ушёл на работу ('has left for work'). Пришёл would mean he arrived here; вошёл is a threshold entry; ходил a completed round trip.

items.promptEnglish: The children walked out of the classroom for the break.
items.hint: Out of a bounded space, briefly.
items.explanation: Exiting the bounded space takes вы-: вышли из класса. The break is a returnable step-out, вы-'s core meaning; пришли is arrival and зашли a drop-in.

items.promptEnglish: Masha walked into the museum and bought a ticket.
items.hint: Into the building, then the next action inside.
items.explanation: The threshold entry takes в-: вошла в музей. The 'и купила' sequence happens just inside the door, which в- frames; пришла would summarize the whole journey.

blanks: Соня _____ из автобуса у школы и пошла к классу. (Sonya got off the bus near the school and went toward her classroom.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: 'Из автобуса' is a small bounded source on a vehicle: the standard verb is выйти. Fem past → вышла. Ушла из автобуса is awkward Russian; пришла из автобуса reverses the source / destination logic; пошла would mark setting off. The 'и пошла к классу' clause confirms the next motion event after the bus exit.

errorCorrection.sentence: Каждое лето наша семья едет на юг к морю.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Every summer our family goes south to the sea.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'Каждое лето' is a habit cue (Step 2): the trip recurs annually, so the round-trip / habit member of the transport pair, ездить (3sg ездит). Едет describes a single one-way trip in progress; ехала would be a past in-progress moment; поехала marks one past departure. The habit frame selects the разно-направленный member.

errorCorrection.sentence: Бабушки сейчас нет дома: она приехала в деревню на всё лето.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Grandma isn't home right now: she has gone off to the village for the whole summer.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'Бабушки нет дома' is an absence frame and 'на всё лето' a long-absence duration: both select у- (gone away from the speaker's location): уехала (Lesson 6). Приехала means arrived (here), which contradicts 'нет дома'. Ехала would describe her in transit at a past moment; ездила a completed round-trip, contradicting the still-away summer. У- reports the subject is gone and not back.

errorCorrection.sentence: Лена открыла дверь и вышла в тёмную комнату.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Lena opened the door and walked into the dark room.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'В комнату' (into the room, в + acc) names a space being entered, so the entry prefix в-: вошла. Вышла is the opposite direction (exit), which contradicts the into-the-room destination. Ушла would mean she left altogether.

minimalPairs.context: Маша _____ домой и сразу легла спать.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha came home and immediately went to bed.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'И сразу легла спать' is a sequence inside the home: Masha is here, she arrived, then she slept. Arrival reading → пришла. Ушла would mean she is gone from the speaker's location, contradicting the in-home sleeping sequence.

minimalPairs.context: Иван _____ из Москвы и привёз подарки.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Ivan arrived from Moscow and brought gifts.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'Привёз подарки' (brought gifts) means the gifts are now with the speaker: Ivan is back. Arrival reading on transport → приехал. Уехал would mean Ivan is gone TO somewhere, with the gifts going with him, which the 'привёз' verb does not allow (привёз = brought here).

patternRecognition.sentence: Маша часто ходит в музей по выходным.
patternRecognition.question: What system is operating here?
patternRecognition.explanation: 'Часто' and 'по выходным' are both habit cues. The bare разно-направленный member of the foot pair is ходить, 3sg ходит. The system at work is the pair choice (Lessons 1 and 2): one-way vs round-trip / habit.

patternRecognition.question: What system is operating here?
patternRecognition.explanation: 'Уже... с работы' is the у- diagnostic pair: уже + a daily-life source phrase, with an absence frame implied. The form ушёл carries the gone-away reading from Lesson 6: Anton is no longer at the speaker's location.

patternRecognition.sentence: Дети вошли в класс и сели на свои места.
patternRecognition.question: What system is operating here?
patternRecognition.explanation: 'И сели на свои места' is a sequence inside the classroom: the next event happens immediately after the threshold-crossing. Plural past of войти → вошли. The system is the entry prefix в- from Lesson 8, which adds the threshold focus that при- does not.

patternRecognition.question: What system is operating here?
patternRecognition.explanation: 'Из Москвы' is the source phrase that pairs with arrival: Ivan is now back, having ended his trip from Moscow. Masc past of приехать → приехал. The system is the arrival prefix при- from Lesson 5, which reports the completion of the trip from the speaker's vantage at the destination.

reviewVocab.definition: The pair-choice: ходить / ездить for a round-trip, habit, or general claim; идти / ехать for a single one-way trip in progress. Choose ходить / идти on foot, ездить / ехать by transport.
reviewVocab.example: Маша часто ходит в музей. Антон сейчас идёт домой.

reviewVocab.definition: The five perfective prefixes on a motion verb: по- (set off), при- (arrived here), у- (gone away), вы- (crossed out), в- (crossed in). Each reports a different moment of the trip.
reviewVocab.example: Антон пошёл / пришёл / ушёл / вышел / вошёл.

reviewVocab.term: в / на + acc, из / с + gen
reviewVocab.definition: Destination phrases в / на + acc (в музей, на работу) and source phrases из / с + gen (из Москвы, с работы). The preposition depends on the type of place.
reviewVocab.example: Иван уехал из Москвы в Петербург. Маша вышла с работы и пошла на лекцию.
